layouts.name: Sega Activator — GPGX sensor channels
layouts.notes: Sixteen native sensor channels, 1L/1U through 8L/8U. Channel-grid schematic, not a physical ring orientation diagram. Each sensor requires independent calibrated input; a regular pad may not have enough controls.

layouts.name: PC Engine — TurboNyma six-button controls
layouts.notes: Native TurboNyma exposes separate edge-triggered selectors for 2-button and 6-button mode, not a toggle. This schematic represents emulator controls; six-button mode requires a compatible game.

layouts.name: Sega SG-1000 — two-button controls
layouts.notes: Generic two-button schematic, not model-specific SG-1000 controller artwork. Native SMSHawk uses six gameplay controls; core console Pause/Reset are separate. Implementation is untested.
layouts.source: BizHawk 8c6b8958bbbe623eaaa36bc82af858b812893628: SMSControllers.cs and SMSControllerDeck.cs; Lunchbox schematic geometry.

layouts.name: Sega Master System — pad and console Pause
layouts.notes: Buttons 1/2 belong to the pad; Pause is a console action exposed by Mednafen on each native input port.

layouts.name: Sega Master System — two-button pad
layouts.notes: D-pad and buttons 1/2 only. Pause and Reset are console controls, not pad buttons. Native SMSHawk adapter integration is incomplete and untested.
layouts.source: BizHawk 8c6b8958bbbe623eaaa36bc82af858b812893628: SMSControllers.cs and SMSControllerDeck.cs; Lunchbox schematic geometry.

layouts.name: NES Power Pad — numbered switches
layouts.notes: Numbered 4-by-3 schematic follows BizHawk's Power Pad schema, not a photographic mat-side depiction. PP1–PP12 are independent digital switches; no joystick directions or gameplay menu buttons are implied. Native NesHawk integration is implemented but untested.

layouts.name: Arcade — six buttons (1 2 3 / 4 5 6)
layouts.source: Lunchbox physical arcade-layout convention; native wiring is defined separately by each emulator profile.
layouts.notes: Street Fighter-style rows: buttons 1/2/3 above 4/5/6. Calibrate physical positions, not printed console button names. Action labels remain game-specific.

layouts.name: Arcade — eight buttons (1 2 3 7 / 4 5 6 8)
layouts.source: Lunchbox physical arcade-layout convention; native wiring is defined separately by each emulator profile.
layouts.notes: Extends the six-button layout with 7/8 in the rightmost column; the first six positions never move. MAME sends the extra physical buttons through frontend L3/R3, not trigger axes.

layouts.name: MAME fixed digital channels
layouts.notes: Per-game discovery selects required controls. Buttons 7/8 use stick clicks, not trigger axes. Analog and peripheral fields require separate contracts.

layouts.name: DualShock 2 — twelve proportional buttons
layouts.notes: Requires independent measured pressure on D-pad, face and shoulder buttons, plus two real bipolar sticks. Digital buttons do not substitute for proportional pressure.

layouts.name: SAME CD-i — left-stick pointer speed
layouts.notes: Native sequence writer maps joystick axes to relative pointer velocity, not absolute position. Sensitivity 100. Three actions include the native buttons-1+2 chord. Configuration routing and launch remain pending.

layouts.name: SAME CD-i — D-pad relative pointer
layouts.notes: Native increment/decrement sequences move the relative pointer with key delta 2 and sensitivity 100. This digital mode does not claim proportional speed. Configuration routing and launch remain pending.

layouts.name: SAME CD-i — relative pointer and button chord
layouts.notes: Source contract; no launch profile yet. The slave consumes relative mouse motion and clamps its accumulated device position to X 0..767 and Y 0..559. Button 3 emits the same protocol bits as buttons 1+2 together, not a third independent wire. The unmodified libretro mouse poller reads only left/right buttons; the combined action needs a reviewed chord route. Physical mouse and controller-driven relative pointer transport remain to be connected.

layouts.name: Dolphin — GameCube analog sticks and mixed triggers
layouts.notes: Guarded raw-GameCube launch contract. Native analog trigger travel supplies both pressure and thresholded click. Digital L2/R2 fallback applies only when the corresponding analog channel is zero. L3/R3 force full analog travel without independently asserting the click. Triforce, microphone and Wii controls are separate. Runtime validation is deferred.

layouts.name: Dolphin native GameCube controller
layouts.notes: Standard native GameCube pad: independent main/C sticks, analog L/R travel and digital L/R clicks. Does not include libretro fallback/full-analog shortcut channels.

layouts.name: ScummVM — RetroPad cursor and keyboard actions
layouts.notes: Pinned core-default semantic map: D-pad and left stick move the cursor; right-stick directions emit arrow keys. L/R are mouse buttons, not A/B. F5/Space/Return/Escape effects depend on the active engine. Launch options must pin all mapper entries before this becomes an enabled contract.

layouts.name: Steem SSE — ST one-fire joystick
layouts.notes: SVN r1501: two frontend ports map in reverse order to ST ports. A and B assert the same fire bit. Physical mouse buttons also share those fire bits. This layout does not imply Hatari jump/autofire shortcuts or verified startup configuration.

layouts.name: SimCoupe — patched one-fire joystick
layouts.notes: Requires Lunchbox's opt-in patched core. A and B both assert the same SAM joystick fire line, not independent fire buttons. This fixed joystick layout does not invoke unfinished reset/menu/mouse shortcuts.

layouts.name: SimCoupe — virtual keyboard navigation
layouts.notes: Preview of the virtual-keyboard UI only. L toggles it on release; D-pad moves the selection on release and A selects a key/action on release. This is not a working joystick/fire contract. Special-key translation and startup configuration remain unresolved.

layouts.name: Hatari ST joystick — jump shortcut
layouts.notes: D-pad and B fire. Y supplies Up through the configured jump shortcut; A is held autofire, not a third independent ST fire button. Frontend port 0 maps to ST port 1 and frontend port 1 maps to ST port 0. Keyboard and mouse remain separate inputs.

layouts.name: Hatari ST joystick — Space shortcut
layouts.notes: D-pad and B fire. Y supplies the core's Space shortcut when jump-on-fire2 is disabled. A is held autofire, not a third independent ST fire button. Space is a shared emulated keyboard input, not a separate per-player fire line.

layouts.name: Nintendo 3DS — Panda3DS standard controls
layouts.notes: Standard buttons and native Circle Pad. Touch requires a separate frontend pointer; C-stick and configuration-dependent Circle Pad Pro buttons are not part of this profile.

layouts.name: Palm m500/m515 — buttons and stick stylus
layouts.notes: m500/m515 have up/down and four hardware application buttons, not a five-way D-pad. Native left stick moves the touchscreen cursor; R holds contact. Graffiti area stays visible.

layouts.name: Macintosh — Mini vMac digital mouse
layouts.notes: Guest Mac receives one mouse button (A). B is GUI-only. Select toggles host/gamepad mouse input; guest and GUI keep separate mode state. D-pad remains needed in the GUI.

layouts.name: Macintosh — Mini vMac left-stick mouse
layouts.notes: Guest Mac receives one mouse button (A). B is GUI-only. Select toggles host/gamepad mouse input; guest and GUI keep separate mode state. D-pad remains needed in the GUI.

layouts.name: BBC Micro — b2 QAOP keyboard
layouts.notes: Fixed guest keys on one pad. A is deliberately unassigned because it also fires the always-active ADC joystick path. No virtual keyboard.

layouts.name: BBC Micro — b2 AZOP keyboard
layouts.notes: Fixed guest keys on one pad. A is deliberately unassigned because it also fires the always-active ADC joystick path. No virtual keyboard.

layouts.name: BBC Micro — b2 analog joystick
layouts.notes: Native left-stick X/Y feed a BBC ADC channel pair; RetroPad A is fire. No digital joystick or keyboard emulation is implied.

layouts.name: ZX Spectrum — ep128emu Sinclair 1
layouts.notes: Keyboard-encoded adapter. Key aliases are shared with the guest keyboard and other adapters, not isolated player inputs.

layouts.name: ZX Spectrum — ep128emu Sinclair 2
layouts.notes: Keyboard-encoded adapter. Key aliases are shared with the guest keyboard and other adapters, not isolated player inputs.

layouts.name: ZX Spectrum — ep128emu Protek
layouts.notes: Keyboard-encoded adapter. Key aliases are shared with the guest keyboard and other adapters, not isolated player inputs.

layouts.name: CPC — ep128emu joystick two
layouts.notes: CPC joystick two shares keyboard matrix contacts: up/down/left/right are 6/5/R/T; fire 1/2 are G/F. The core ORs active inputs during keyboard conversion. No player-one system shortcuts on this port.

layouts.name: ep128emu — one-fire joystick
layouts.notes: Source-derived target: directions plus RetroPad X primary fire. Joystick-only layout for ports without player-one shortcuts. Configuration resolution is required before selecting this layout for launch.

layouts.name: ep128emu — one-fire joystick and player-one shortcuts
layouts.notes: Source-derived target: directions plus RetroPad X primary fire. Includes hardcoded player-one shortcuts before configuration overrides. Configuration resolution is required before selecting this layout for launch.

layouts.name: ep128emu — two-fire joystick
layouts.notes: Source-derived target: directions plus RetroPad X primary fire and A secondary fire (CPC). Joystick-only layout for ports without player-one shortcuts. Configuration resolution is required before selecting this layout for launch.

layouts.name: ep128emu — two-fire joystick and player-one shortcuts
layouts.notes: Source-derived target: directions plus RetroPad X primary fire and A secondary fire (CPC). Includes hardcoded player-one shortcuts before configuration overrides. Configuration resolution is required before selecting this layout for launch.

layouts.name: PC-98 — NP2kai digital mouse
layouts.notes: D-pad relative mouse motion and B/A left/right click. L3 opens the core menu.

layouts.name: PC-98 — NP2kai left-stick mouse
layouts.notes: D-pad relative mouse motion and B/A left/right click. The selected native stick also moves the pointer; press it for left click or hold L2 while pressing it for right click. The other stick button opens the menu.

layouts.name: PC-98 — NP2kai right-stick mouse
layouts.notes: D-pad relative mouse motion and B/A left/right click. The selected native stick also moves the pointer; press it for left click or hold L2 while pressing it for right click. The other stick button opens the menu.

layouts.name: PC-98 — NP2kai Arrows keyboard preset
layouts.notes: Twelve fixed keyboard mappings and an L3 core-menu shortcut. These keyboard modes replace normal physical-keyboard polling; the menu is not a virtual keyboard.

layouts.name: PC-98 — NP2kai Arrows 3button keyboard preset
layouts.notes: Twelve fixed keyboard mappings and an L3 core-menu shortcut. These keyboard modes replace normal physical-keyboard polling; the menu is not a virtual keyboard.

layouts.name: X68000 — analog Cyberstick and system shortcuts
layouts.notes: Native left X/Y and reversed right-stick Y feed three unsigned eight-bit Cyberstick axes. D-pad is retained for core-menu navigation, not analog joystick motion. Independent miniature lever buttons are not exposed by this core path.

layouts.name: X68000 — Default (2 Buttons) — gameplay only

layouts.name: X68000 — CPSF-MD (8 Buttons) — gameplay only

layouts.notes: Primary pad sends fixed keyboard keys. Hold L or R and use Left/Right to choose a disk for the corresponding drive; release the shoulder to insert it. Keyboard input is paused during disk selection.

layouts.name: PC-8801 — QUASI88 second-pad keys
layouts.notes: The second pad sends R/F/D/G, Q and Tab keyboard keys, not a separate joystick device.

layouts.name: Amiga — D-pad mouse and keyboard
layouts.notes: Three mouse buttons and speed modifiers. D-pad supplies relative mouse motion; no native stick is required. Keyboard shortcuts are owned by player one.

layouts.name: Amiga — analog-stick mouse and keyboard
layouts.notes: Three mouse buttons and speed modifiers. Native left stick provides proportional mouse motion; D-pad also moves the mouse. Keyboard shortcuts are owned by player one.

layouts.name: Amiga CD32 — seven-button gamepad and keyboard
layouts.notes: CD32's four colored buttons, two transport shoulders and Play/Pause. Select is a frontend virtual-keyboard shortcut owned by player one, not a CD32 hardware button.

layouts.name: Amiga — two-button joystick and keyboard
layouts.notes: Two fire buttons and digital directions. Player one owns virtual-keyboard and Return shortcuts; later players expose only joystick controls. Physical mouse input is disabled in these fixed joystick modes.

layouts.name: DOSBox Pure — two independent two-button joysticks
layouts.notes: Joystick numbering follows player assignment: frontend port one drives DOS joystick one, frontend port two drives DOS joystick two. Keyboard and menu controls belong only to player one; player two uses directions, two buttons and the native left stick.

layouts.notes: Explicit fixed preset with core menu enabled on L3. Labels include collision-shifted generic keyboard fallback. Native mouse/joystick axes retain analog transport; keyboard axis pairs use the core's signed 12000 threshold.

layouts.name: DOSBox Pure — Both DOS joysticks + keyboard
layouts.notes: Explicit fixed preset with core menu enabled on L3. Labels include collision-shifted generic keyboard fallback. Native mouse/joystick axes retain analog transport; keyboard axis pairs use the core's signed 12000 threshold.

layouts.name: DOSBox Pure — generic keyboard / direct F1–F2
layouts.notes: Fixed port-one generic-keyboard preset. Native stick axes produce keyboard pairs, not proportional DOS joystick motion. L3/R3 send F1/F2; no gamepad menu shortcut.

layouts.name: DOSBox Pure — generic keyboard with menu
layouts.notes: Fixed port-one generic-keyboard preset. Native stick axes produce keyboard pairs, not proportional DOS joystick motion. L3 opens the overlay, F1 shifts to R3 and F2 loses its direct shortcut.

layouts.name: Atari 8-bit — joystick, console and keyboard
layouts.notes: Player one owns console keys and the virtual keyboard. Other players use directions and Fire only. The overlay navigates and selects on button release. Unmodified Atari joysticks have one Fire button; Joy 2B+ is a separate mode.

layouts.name: Atari 5200 — digital input and full keypad overlay
layouts.notes: Single-player 5200 mapping. Direct keypad shortcuts cover #, *, 0/1/2/3/7; all digits plus Reset are reachable through the keyboard overlay. This does not claim independently routed multiplayer keypad/second-fire state.

layouts.name: Atari 5200 — analog input and full keypad overlay
layouts.notes: Single-player 5200 mapping. Direct keypad shortcuts cover #, *, 0/1/2/3/7; all digits plus Reset are reachable through the keyboard overlay. This does not claim independently routed multiplayer keypad/second-fire state.

layouts.name: Elektronika BK — four-button joystick
layouts.notes: Four directions and four independent joystick buttons on the BK UP port. This is not keyboard emulation; keyboard-driven programs still need a physical keyboard. Both frontend joypads are ORed into the same hardware register, so only one is assigned.

layouts.name: ZX81 — cursor keys and keyboard overlay
layouts.notes: One joypad supplies explicitly mapped ZX81 keys and operates the keyboard overlay. A/B select overlay keys; Shift is available directly and as a toggle in the overlay. The second frontend port is reserved for a physical keyboard, not another joystick.

layouts.name: ZX81 — QAOP and keyboard overlay
layouts.notes: One joypad supplies explicitly mapped ZX81 keys and operates the keyboard overlay. A/B select overlay keys; Shift is available directly and as a toggle in the overlay. The second frontend port is reserved for a physical keyboard, not another joystick.

layouts.name: CrocoDS — joystick, keyboard and menu
layouts.notes: One frontend pad: directions and two fire buttons, Return, numeric shortcuts and core UI actions. The native Linux resolver checks the combined global and per-content input configuration before this fixed layout is applied.

layouts.name: CPC Caprice32 — Joystick and keyboard shortcuts
layouts.notes: Select is a held command modifier, not an independent game key while held. Select+Start toggles the core virtual keyboard; D-pad moves its cursor and A clicks. Select+face/directions/shoulders dispatch core loader or disk commands. Source-grounded; not runtime-tested.

layouts.name: CPC Caprice32 — QAOP keyboard controls
layouts.notes: Select is a held command modifier, not an independent game key while held. Select+Start toggles the core virtual keyboard; D-pad moves its cursor and A clicks. Select+face/directions/shoulders dispatch core loader or disk commands. Source-grounded; not runtime-tested.

layouts.name: CPC Caprice32 — Incentive keyboard controls
layouts.notes: Select is a held command modifier, not an independent game key while held. Select+Start toggles the core virtual keyboard; D-pad moves its cursor and A clicks. Select+face/directions/shoulders dispatch core loader or disk commands. Source-grounded; not runtime-tested.

layouts.name: CPC Caprice32 — Two joystick ports and virtual keyboard
layouts.notes: Select is a held command modifier, not an independent game key while held. Select+Start toggles the core virtual keyboard; D-pad moves its cursor and A clicks. Select+face/directions/shoulders dispatch core loader or disk commands. Source-grounded; not runtime-tested.

layouts.name: VICE — joystick and controller-operated keyboard
layouts.notes: One-button joystick directions/Fire plus VICE virtual-keyboard navigation, selection, ShiftLock, transparency, Space and Return. While the overlay is visible, the same controls operate it. This is not arbitrary physical-keyboard remapping.

layouts.name: VICE — controller-operated virtual keyboard
layouts.notes: Keyboard-only gaming workflow for PET: open the core keyboard, navigate with directions and press the selected key. Does not imply an emulated joystick port. Space and Return are direct shortcuts.

layouts.name: Jaguar — full keypad using two analog sticks
layouts.notes: All 12 keypad keys plus directions, A/B/C, Pause and Option. Core-thresholded stick directions supply 7/8/9/*/#; opposite directions on one axis cannot be held simultaneously. This is an explicit gamepad workflow, not independent keypad switches or analog Jaguar hardware.

layouts.name: MAME — twin digital sticks
layouts.notes: Independent digital direction clusters. Right directions use native buttons 4/1/3/2. Up to six observed actions among native buttons 1-16 use switches 5-8 followed by the L2/R2 axis-threshold switches, allocated in native action-number order. The derived logical panel includes all sixteen action identities, not sixteen independent output channels or physical cabinet geometry. Only observed controls are required.

layouts.name: Twin Stick — two physical analog sticks
layouts.notes: Two proportional input sticks for a core-owned analog-to-digital conversion, plus four digital hand controls, Start and Special. This input requirement does not claim that the emulated Twin Stick has analog hardware.

layouts.name: Dreamcast — twin digital sticks
layouts.notes: Two independent four-way digital clusters, one trigger and turbo control per hand, Start and Special. The emulated Twin Stick advertises no proportional axes; turbo buttons are game inputs, not synthesized autofire.

layouts.name: Dreamcast — six-button arcade stick
layouts.notes: Digital arcade stick with A/B/C and X/Y/Z rows, Start and four directions. No Genesis Mode button, analog stick or proportional triggers are implied.

layouts.name: Dreamcast — proportional stick and triggers
layouts.notes: Dreamcast controller target with independent proportional L/R triggers. A digital shoulder button cannot satisfy either trigger capability; native range calibration and output normalization are required.

layouts.name: Dreamcast — legacy Redream digital-trigger pad
layouts.notes: Legacy libretro Redream controller callback: proportional main stick, D-pad, A/B/X/Y and Start, but L/R trigger values are reduced to binary released/full endpoints. Not a claim of full Dreamcast analog-trigger fidelity.

layouts.name: J2ME vendor mode — navigation and keypad subset
layouts.notes: Vendor modes send dedicated navigation codes for the four directions. Numeric 2/4/6/8 are not emitted by this joypad path; the other numeric keys, star/hash and soft keys retain distinct targets.

layouts.name: J2ME vendor mode — navigation, keypad subset and pointer
layouts.notes: Vendor modes send dedicated navigation codes for the four directions. Numeric 2/4/6/8 are not emitted by this joypad path; the other numeric keys, star/hash and soft keys retain distinct targets. Keypad 5 becomes click while the analog pointer is visible.

layouts.name: J2ME Standard — numeric keypad and soft keys
layouts.notes: Standard phone mode sends numeric 2/8/4/6 for directional inputs, not vendor navigation keycodes. All twelve numeric/star/hash keys and both soft keys are independent digital targets.

layouts.name: J2ME Standard — keypad and right-stick pointer
layouts.notes: Standard keypad plus proportional right-stick pointer motion. Keypad 5 becomes pointer-click while the core's analog pointer is visible; it is not an independent simultaneous click and keypad key.

layouts.name: Odyssey² / Videopac — joystick and virtual keyboard
layouts.notes: Digital joystick with player-one virtual keyboard and numeric shortcuts. Console keyboard actions are frontend-port-one controls, independent of emulated joystick-side swapping.

layouts.name: Super Cassette Vision — controllers and console keypad
layouts.notes: Four joystick directions and independent left/right fire buttons, with a shared controller-operated console keypad. Enter/both-fire is a core-provided compound action; Pause, Reset, Power and numeric keys are selected in the overlay.

layouts.name: Atari 2600 — joystick and console panel
layouts.notes: Joystick directions and Fire with player-one console switches. Optional Trigger/Booster are separate physical pins used only by the selected Genesis, BoosterGrip or Joy2B+ contract; they are not extra buttons on a stock Atari joystick.

layouts.name: ColecoVision — JollyCV shifted keypad and Super Action
layouts.notes: Core-facing shifted-keypad workflow with four action colors and digital spinner steps. Keypad numbers use held modifiers; this is not the independent-key wiring of the standard ColecoVision schematic.

layouts.name: Intellivision — FreeIntv disc and keypad controls
layouts.notes: Core-facing controller workflow: analog disc angle, digital disc navigation, three action buttons, analog keypad shortcuts and a held-button keypad overlay. Analog axes preserve the core's own quantization; this schematic does not claim direct independent wiring of every keypad key.

layouts.name: Channel F — eight-action hand controller
layouts.notes: Four directional movements, push/pull and clockwise/counterclockwise rotation are independent digital actions. The two auxiliary controls operate FreeChaF's console overlay and controller swap, not physical console switches directly.

layouts.name: ColecoVision — joystick, side buttons and keypad
layouts.notes: Standard controller schematic with four directions, two independent side buttons and twelve keypad keys. All are digital; core-specific analog-axis encodings for keypad keys do not change that capability requirement.

layouts.name: ZX Spectrum — single-fire joystick
layouts.notes: One fire button and four directions. The chosen Spectrum interface determines the emulated joystick protocol; this is not an exact vendor shell.

layouts.name: Spectravideo — single-fire joystick
layouts.notes: One fire input and four independent digital directions. Functional schematic, not exact shell geometry; no second trigger is exposed by the standard SVI joystick.

layouts.name: MSX — predefined keyboard gamepad
layouts.notes: Functional keyboard-key clusters for the fMSX Emulated Keyboard device. This is not a full keyboard or physical keycap layout. Directions are keyboard arrow keys, not joystick directions.

layouts.name: MSX — two-trigger joystick
layouts.notes: Six-input joystick schematic. MSX controllers vary in shell geometry. Keyboard input is a separate interface.

layouts.name: MSX — joystick and keyboard shortcuts
layouts.notes: MSX joystick plus ten explicit keyboard keys exposed by the fMSX combined device. This is a functional schematic, not a complete keyboard or vendor controller.

layouts.name: Nintendo DS/DSi — melonDS stick stylus and modifier
layouts.notes: DS buttons and core-specific relative stylus controls. Modifier changes pointer speed; Modifier+Y toggles the lid and still sends Y to the console. Mic noise is simulated, not speech input.

layouts.name: Nintendo DS — buttons, lid and stick-driven stylus
layouts.notes: Native DS button schematic plus emulator stylus and panel actions. Stylus axes are either cursor velocity or stick-to-coordinate positioning according to the selected profile, not native console analog sticks. Microphone action generates a noise pattern, not voice capture.

layouts.name: Nintendo 3DS — gamepad and stick-driven touch cursor
layouts.notes: The right analog cluster is a relative touch-cursor velocity control supplied by this core, not a second native console stick or absolute touchscreen. Hold Touch press while moving to drag.

layouts.name: Nintendo 3DS — gamepad controls
layouts.notes: Gameplay-control schematic, not a touchscreen or exact shell drawing. Circle Pad and C-stick are proportional axes. Touch, motion, microphone and Home are separate interfaces.

layouts.name: New Nintendo 3DS — gamepad controls
layouts.notes: Gameplay-control schematic, not a touchscreen or exact shell drawing. Circle Pad and C-stick are proportional axes. Touch, motion, microphone and Home are separate interfaces.

layouts.name: Arduboy — A/B and directions
layouts.notes: Six-input gameplay schematic, not exact shell dimensions. Hardware reset, power, serial/link and debugger actions are not gameplay buttons.

Start-in-analog mode is explicitly enabled. The core promotes an unlocked digital pad once after reset; subsequent game-driven mode changes and locks remain effective. No separate host Analog toggle is invented.
Requires a fresh start; loading a save state can restore different controller state. BIOS, media loading and game compatibility remain independent requirements.

The normalized transport requires existing writable /dev/uinput access. Physical force-feedback forwarding is not implemented, so rumble is explicitly disabled. USB mouse/keyboard, combined USB modes and other peripherals remain unfinished.

D-pad sends relative mouse motion; opposite directions cancel. A is the guest Mac's single mouse button. B is not delivered as a guest right click: it is useful only in the core GUI.
Native left-stick movement adds relative mouse motion after a 15% deadzone, scaled to about 50 units per poll at full deflection. The GUI's pointer path uses D-pad, so D-pad is still required.

L toggles the keyboard overlay; Start opens the disk-file GUI under the selected 513 device. GUI mouse-source state is separate and also starts in host-mouse mode; use Select there when necessary. When an overlay and guest polling both run, Select can change both states, so check pointer response after closing it.

The source does not implement the README's claimed shoulder disk flips, speed shortcut or guest joystick behavior in this path; they are not mapped. The live frame loop calls retro_poll_event with joystick delivery disabled.

Only player one is polled for these controls. Physical keyboard uses the Poll option and remains available outside the overlay. Overlay presence does not establish complete modifier/keyboard fidelity. Release mouse buttons before changing source or opening/closing the GUI.
Direct DSK/IMG entrypoints only. Commands, archives, other disk formats, firmware and boot compatibility remain separate work.

Fixed Master 128 (MOS 3.20) model supplies an ADC. Each controller's native left X/Y feeds its channel pair (0/1 or 2/3); RetroPad A sends that joystick's fire button. D-pad does not substitute for analog motion.

The core converts axes using (32767 - value) >> 6. Axis state is delivered only when it changes; move each stick and return it to center after startup before relying on centered ADC values. Do not switch machine models or reset/reload the core while relying on this launch's initialized input state.

All 24 joypad-to-key assignments, including both sticks' direction-to-key mappings, are cleared in private options. Physical keyboard remains necessary for guest commands and keyboard-only games. No virtual keyboard or digital joystick is claimed.
The controller-device callback has no active remapping logic. The live ADC path polls exactly two ports; the commented digital joystick implementation is not exposed as working hardware.
Direct SSD/DSD disk content only. Autoboot preference is preserved; bracketed filename autorun behavior belongs to the core. Firmware, disk boot and game compatibility remain separate prerequisites.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · ep128emu · TVC default joysticks
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

Default mapping: port 1 internal directions and Space; ports 2/3 external joysticks 1/2; ports 4/5 GameCard external joysticks 3/4. Primary fire is RetroPad X. The sixth default frontend mapping (external 5) has no TVC hardware path and is not offered.

Internal and external joystick 1 share directions in the TVC keyboard matrix; their fire inputs differ (Space versus joystick fire). These are not five independent player devices. GameCard ports 0x32/0x33 require software that reads them; this does not promise multiplayer or ROM compatibility.

Player one also sends Enter and keys 0–3. L3 shows mapping information and R3 fits the image to content. Physical keyboard is still necessary for other keys; no virtual keyboard is claimed. External joystick secondary fire is not mapped by this core's TVC initialization.

TVCWAV with a RIFF/WAVE header or CRT with a MOPS signature selects TVC64. Cartridges are installed into ROM segment 1 by the core. Native RetroArch and an explicit existing system_directory are required. System-wide TVC config, content sidecar and all four machine markers must be absent; they and the media header are checked again before launch. Existing user files are preserved.

Private options fix information/zoom and disable autofire; device callbacks consistently rebuild defaults. Do not change input options or devices during the session. Disk, direct-file and custom mappings remain separate work.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · ep128emu · ZX default adapters
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

Four default adapter mappings, not four independent players: port 1 Kempston, port 2 Sinclair 1, port 3 Sinclair 2 and port 4 Protek. Select the matching adapter in the guest software. Primary fire is RetroPad X.

The Sinclair/Protek layouts show their exact number-key aliases. Use only the adapter needed by the game: simultaneous aliases can interfere. The core tracks transitions per frontend port without aggregating shared source keys; releasing one port can release a key held by another. Player-one number-key shortcuts also share those keys.

Port one additionally sends Enter and 0–3, with L3 mapping information and R3 fit-to-content. Other ports have joystick controls only. Physical keyboard remains necessary for other input; no virtual keyboard is claimed.

TZX v1 content selects ZX128 tape mode. TAP content is accepted only when its first three bytes match the core's ZX heuristic: first byte 0x0f–0x21, second zero, third zero or 0xff; this selects ZX128 direct-file mode. Other TAP content can select Enterprise and is rejected. Native RetroArch, an explicit existing system_directory and absence of system-wide ZX config, content sidecar and all four content-directory machine markers are required. Paths and header are checked again before launch; user files are preserved.

Private options fix information/zoom and disable autofire; generic device callbacks consistently rebuild defaults. Do not change input options or devices during the session. Other machine models and custom mappings remain separate work; firmware and boot compatibility are not established.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · ep128emu · Enterprise default joysticks
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

Default Enterprise topology: player one uses the internal joystick (cursor keys and Space); players two through six use external joysticks 1 through 5. Primary fire is RetroPad X. External 3/5 fire overlaps external 1 fire 2/3; external 4 fire overlaps external 2 fire 2. These rare adapters require software support; six mapped ports do not imply six-player games or isolated multi-button joystick hardware.

Player one also sends Enter and keys 0–3. L3 shows mapping information; R3 fits the image to content. Other ports have joystick controls only. Physical keyboard input remains available and necessary for other keys; no controller-operated virtual keyboard is claimed.

Native ep128emu TAP content with its eight-byte format signature selects Enterprise 128 tape mode. EPT has a detection branch but is not advertised in the core's valid_extensions, so it is not a launch entrypoint here. Other tape formats, disk/file routes, machine variants and custom adapter assignments remain separate work.

Native RetroArch with an explicit existing system_directory is required. The system-wide Enterprise configuration, per-game sidecar and all four machine markers beside the content must be absent. These paths and the header are rechecked before launch; user files are preserved.

Generic device callbacks consistently rebuild defaults. Private options fix information/zoom buttons and disable autofire. Do not change core input options or devices during the session. Firmware, boot and software compatibility remain separate prerequisites.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · PX68k · analog Cyberstick
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

First port is fixed to Cyberstick (Analog). The core converts native left X/Y to unsigned eight-bit axes and reverses right-stick Y for the third axis. Right-stick X is not consumed. Two native sticks are required; digital D-pad input does not synthesize analog motion.
Face controls A/B/X/Y send Cyberstick A/B/C/D. L/R send E1/E2; Start/Select send F/G. Independent miniature lever buttons are not exposed by this core path.
D-pad provides core-menu navigation. L2 opens the menu using F12 and R2 sends the registration key via Scroll Lock; only player one owns these shortcuts.
Private options are reapplied after legacy configuration loading, with default Select keyboard mapping and unswapped trigger order. Do not change input modes in the core menu.
AnalogState is shared and Cyberstick is a first-port option only. A second controller, when explicitly selected, uses a standard or CPSF adapter rather than another Cyberstick.
Direct floppy entrypoints only; command files, playlists, hard disks and firmware/boot verification remain separate work. Physical keyboard or mouse may still be required.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · QUASI88 · N88 V2 fixed keyboard controls
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

Both pads use the core's fixed keyboard mappings. Player one uses keypad 8/2/4/6 with Z/X, Shift, Space, Return and I; player two uses R/F/D/G with Q/Tab. Per-port target layouts preserve these different key labels.

Start sends the core's three Return key variants together. The generic controller-device callback is empty; clearing unused physical bindings is what prevents inherited input, not assuming that device selection changes the hard-coded mapping.

Player one holds L for drive 1 or R for drive 2, uses Left/Right to choose an image, then releases the shoulder to insert it. The core skips other input polling during this selector: release gameplay keys before swapping disks.

The guest must use these keyboard bindings. This does not claim native joystick input: the later PAD1/PAD2 code calls the keyboard polling helper rather than polling either joypad. Physical keyboard input remains necessary for other keys; there is no claimed controller-operated keyboard overlay.

Fixed BASIC mode N88 V2. Required ROMs and software compatibility are separate prerequisites. N-BASIC may be used by PC-8000 software, but this profile does not add an unverified PC-8000 platform alias.

Direct D88 media only. Paths containing lowercase .m3u are rejected because the core routes them to its playlist loader regardless of the final extension. Playlist and subsystem entrypoints need separate handling.

emulator_profiles.name: RetroArch · PUAE · A500OG D-pad mouse
conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred.

Fixed A500OG model, explicit device 257 and private mouse mode avoid Automatic model/device substitution and in-session mouse toggling. Six frontend slots are accounted for; at most two pads drive separate emulated mouse ports.

B/A supply left/right click, Y explicitly supplies middle click, L2 slows and R2 accelerates mouse motion. D-pad speed is fixed to 6 (the core's 100% setting); physical mouse input is disabled to prevent competing mouse sources.
Native stick mouse motion is disabled; this mode uses D-pad relative motion and does not require an analog stick.

Player one owns Select for the virtual keyboard and Start for Return. Player two has only mouse controls. Guest software must support the selected mouse port(s); the second mouse is not automatically a second player in every application.
Private mapper and keyboard hotkeys are fixed. Do not change mouse/joystick mode or controller device during the session. Keyboard passthrough remains enabled for typing.

The native save-directory guard snapshots model/global/content UAE files and preserves user settings. Substantive overrides, default save paths and Flatpak namespaces still need effective-input adapters.
Direct floppy entrypoints only. Hard disks, playlists, archives and custom UAE files remain separate work; required firmware and boot compatibility are not established by this mapping.

conditions: Source-grounded implementation; builds and runtime verification are deferred. Coleco BIOS and game compatibility remain separate requirements.
